Flanders Fields is a common English name of the World War I battlefields in an area straddling the Belgian provinces of West Flanders and East Flanders as well as the French department of Nord-Pas-de-Calais.

The name is particularly associated with battles that took place in the Ypres Salient, including the Second Battle of Ypres and the Battle of Passchendaele, and was known as the Western Front. The fields were unmaintained for years before they were made into a war cemetery and memorial. Today Flanders Fields is home to thousands of poppies.

The phrase "In Flanders Fields" originates from a poem titled In Flanders Fields by Canadian physician Lieutenant-Colonel John McCrae, inspired by his service during the Second Battle of Ypres. The poem and poppy are prominent Remembrance Day symbols throughout the Commonwealth, particularly in Canada, where "In Flanders Fields" is one of the nation's best-known literary works. The poem also has wide exposure in the United States, where it is associated with Memorial Day.
